units.text: A leaker with a mixed but usually better than average track record, is now making the absurd claim of having already handled the iPhone 18 Pro Max in a store, and has made a video to back it up. The problem is, demo units aren't in stores yet, and won't be for some time.

With such a short time to go before Apple unveils its new iPhones, there's already been a carrier posting optimistic details of the lineup. Now leaker yeux1122 has posted a video purporting to show them using the iPhone 18 Pro Max in a store.
Specifically, they use the Dark Cherry version and a light blue one. They then compare their existing iPhone 17 Pro Max to the pair of them, all in 14 seconds.
That time raises the Bigfoot question. If you have a camera and Bigfoot in front of you, you don't just take one shot or record a few seconds.
Left: of course a store will display iPhones from the back. Right: of course fakers won't show an iPhone turned on - images credit: yeuz1122.

You also don't only film when its back is turned. This video does briefly show the front screen of one of the iPhones, but of course it's off. And of course a store mounts its demo models with the screen facing the mount.
A lot of effort

Beside the backward-facing display mount in this video, there is a reasonably well-produced retail price sticker. It says that these models being shown have 256GB of storage, and lists a price for them both.

That price appears to be for monthly hire purchase in Russian rubles. If so, it converts to around $123 per month, or more than double what the current 256GB iPhone 17 Pro Max costs per month in the US.
Apple doesn't sell iPhones in Russia, only third-party resellers do, so it's quite possible that the price is higher than anywhere else. That's the only legitimate thing about this video.
But this is just another fake and we can expect more of them in the run up to the announcement on September 9, 2026.

6d69c0d6c8563a2cd1a41922.title: Trying to squeeze more profit out of the App Store is a bad idea

units.text: A new report says that Phil Schiller left the App Store because Apple aims to make more money from it. Read the room, Apple.

Phil Schiller remains with the company as an Apple Fellow, but he recently left his roles as head of events and the App Store. Now according to Bloomberg, a reason for his leaving the App Store was that he doesn't want any part in what's coming to it.
Why Apple legend Phil Schiller is moving to special projects and dropping his roles https://t.co/gRCVldPqyM pic.twitter.com/1w1S0LEXWl
— Mark Gurman (@markgurman) September 6, 2026
It's said that John Ternus and Eddy Cue intend to increase App Store revenues. But there are only practical two ways to do that, and neither can end well for the company, or for its users.
Conceivably Apple could somehow make the App Store suddenly more popular, and maybe launching a Home Hub would help that. Maybe Apple could introduce more ads, as it now has with Apple Maps.
But in practice Apple either raises its commission fees, or it cuts the costs of the App Store.
Raising prices is off the table

Never the calmest of Apple critics, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney might burst a blood vessel if Apple raised any App Store fees. That would be his problem, of course, except that governments do seem to listen to him.

This is especially so in the European Union, where Apple is continually proposing new and lower App Store fees, but Sweeney wants everything to be free. There is a problem that the EU's Digital Markets Act (DMA) is vague enough on these issues that lawyers are being kept well employed, but it will be resolved at some point.
It just cannot be resolved in the EU in any way that sees Apple raising prices. And increasing fees isn't going to cut it in the US, either.

Apple is currently appealing to the Supreme Court about a Ninth Circuit court denied a rehearing over App Store fees. That original Ninth Circuit court ruling in theory allows Apple to collect commissions on outside payments, but in practice the sum requires agreement from Epic Games for some reason.

Apple can of course try raising its App Store prices, but it would be reneging on international agreements. Whatever added revenue it managed to get would probably be short-lived as regulators stepped back in.
Cutting costs is not an option
The problem with cost-cutting is that Apple's not going to suddenly get a better deal on its servers. Instead, cutting App Store costs has to mean cutting jobs.
It's got to be costly employing the App Review team that Apple currently has, but that team already seems unfit for purpose. It needs more people and so more money, not less.
Perhaps Apple is just throwing up its hands and acknowledging that App Review isn't working. Maybe Apple has decided it's lost the fight and that third-party app stores are coming.
Maybe Apple is right. But as long as it continues harping on about being the only line of defense against malware and bad actors for app users, it should at least keep trying.
Where Phil Schiller fits in

Neither Schiller nor Apple have commented, of course, but the account of him leaving over this issue fits with earlier reports over his insistence on human curation. Back in September 2022, he was reported to resisted moves to change the store.
Specifically, he is said to have mandated that apps were chosen to be highlighted by the editorial team, not by letting developers pay.
So with him gone, perhaps this is where Apple thinks it can get some more cash out of developers, by charging them to be promoted.
That wouldn't be increasing fees and it shouldn't have any impact on App Review. But it would immediately stop the App Store's highlights being of any use at all.
If developers can pay to be featured in the App Store's highlights pages, those pages are no longer highlights. They are a list of which developers have the greatest budgets.
Apple talks up how the App Store is for users, but all of its possible moves to increase revenue will be damaging.

e0ef44de52b202a3208421f6.title: Desktop Mac buyer's gude: Which Mac to buy in fall 2026

units.text: Apple's unexpected August update to the Mac mini and Mac Studio has changed the pricing of the models in a big way. Here's the best desktop Mac you should buy for your budget in fall 2026.

In August, while the world was preparing for the expected launch of new iPhone models in September, Apple had a trick up its sleeve. Without any warning, it launched changes to the Mac mini and Mac Studio near the end of August.

Chiefly, the change was to introduce a new M6 chip generation in the Mac mini, as well as to upgrade the Mac Studio to include M5 Max and M5 Ultra versions. Thanks to the ongoing memory chip crisis, this has also meant changes to the way the models are sold.
This guide will aim to help you decide where you should put your budget if you're in the market for a new desktop Mac in September 2026.
Overall desktop Mac range
Apple has just three models of desktop Mac available to purchase. There's the consumer-friendly Mac mini, the 24-inch iMac, and the performance-focused Mac Studio.

As is typical for Apple, anyone buying its products can choose from a selection of configurations, including the amount of memory and storage is available. In some cases, you can even select your preferred wired network speed.
For the purposes of this article, we are breaking the three product lines into six tiers.
The complete price range of Apple's current Macs, as of September 2026
For the Mac mini and Mac Studio, this is easily handled by pricing based on the chip category, that is M6 or M5 Pro for the Mac mini, M5 Max and M5 Ultra for the Mac Studio.
The 24-inch iMac is also split into two versions, referring to the number of Thunderbolt 4 ports each has. That's because there's also other subtle changes at play that are worth taking into account.

The overall price range for desktop Macs starts at $899 for the cheapest configuration of Mac mini, rising to $18,299 for the current most expensive configuration of Mac Studio. This does not include the Mac Studio's potential 512GB memory configuration, which Apple has yet to publish pricing for.
Mac mini (2026)
The Mac mini with an M6 or M5 Pro chip has a Neural Accelerator in each GPU core.

As usual, we will discuss this in two price ranges: Sub-$2,500 for budget purchases, and $2,500 or more for premium options.
Storage and memory upgrades
There are two big drivers of price changes for Apple's lineup. One is memory, and the other is storage.

With the ongoing memory chip crisis affecting the cost of components across the board, that has meant some changes in price apply. Everything's more expensive, but our advice to you doesn't really change at all.

The first of the two, memory, is a factor that can directly affect the performance of your Mac. Since Apple uses Unified Memory, whatever memory you choose affects the main processing as well as the GPU and AI processing capabilities.
You can get away with using the base amount of memory in your Mac's configuration. However, AppleInsider advises to try and pay for a higher level where possible, especially on the Mac mini.

Be aware that this can get expensive quickly. While going from 16GB to 32GB may only be a $400 price difference on the Mac mini, it's an eye-watering $4,000 to go from 96GB to 256GB on the Mac Studio.
Though Apple hasn't said how much 512GB will cost, it could be double that of the 256GB upgrade.

Also, Apple's structuring of model configurations may mean that you won't get some higher memory options with some chip configurations, but you do on other premium setups. In some cases, you may only get one memory option at all.
Storage price levels for Apple's desktop Macs, as of September 2026
The other big price changer, storage, is equally as damaging to the wallet. Sure, it's just $200 to go from 256GB to 512GB of storage on a Mac mini, but it soon gets expensive.
Going from 1TB to 16TB of storage on the Mac Studio is a $7,500 jump in cost.
As usual, the AppleInsider recommendation is to be more willing to pay for the memory upgrade over the storage upgrade.
We have preached about the advantages of external storage as a Mac upgrade for some time. Using the fast Thunderbolt speeds and suitable external storage drives, you can get comparable performance.
Apple doesn't make memory or storage user-serviceable in a remotely realistic manner. The typical user is not going to be able to add more to the internal storage or memory after purchase.
At the very least, external storage is an option for consumers. That's why paying for extra memory should be more of a priority over extra storage.
Even if you can afford it, you should still think twice about buying more storage at the more extreme end of the range.
Under $2,500: Mac mini and 24-inch iMac

The battle for your wallet starts, as always, with the Mac mini with M6. The base configuration at $899 includes the 12-core CPU, 12-core GPU, the dual 16-core Neural Engine, 16GB of memory, 256GB of storage, and 2.5Gb Ethernet.
It's the only one to consider for the first couple of steps, with the changes being memory, storage, and a $100 upgrade to 10Gb Ethernet.
The first real choice is at $1,099, where you should choose the memory upgrade to 24GB over the storage upgrade to 512GB, unless capacity is more important to you.
Desktop Mac price ranges below $2,500, as of September 2026
At $1,299, that Mac mini could have both those smaller upgrades, or you could go for 32GB of memory instead. Either's appropriate here.
The first real decision between models comes in at $1,499, as the two-Thunderbolt port version of the iMac enters the conversation. Though really, it shouldn't be a consideration.

In previous years, we would've argued that you could justify getting a better Mac mini and a display for the same money, unless you really care about aesthetics. That's a situation that's even more apparent this time around.

The iMac is still on M4, making it two generations behind. Add in that the two-port iMac doesn't have a Nano-texture glass option, only supports one external display, and that Ethernet is a payable add-on, and it's not a great purchase at all.
M4 iMac
The M4 iMac has a 24-inch 4.5K Retina display and comes in seven colors.
Buy at Amazon
Buy at B&H

Instead, go for the M6 Mac mini and get both the 32GB of memory and 512GB upgrade, or the base model and spend the difference on a display. Either's a better option than the iMac.
At $1,699, it becomes a four-horse race. For the M6 Mac, you could get the 24GB memory, 1TB storage upgrade, and Ethernet, and you'd be sitting pretty.

However, as well as the lower-tier iMac, there's the upper-tier one as well, with four Thunderbolt ports, a slightly better M4 chip with a few more cores, better external display support, and Gigabit Ethernet as standard.
That all said, it's kinda the same situation again. A Mac mini with a display is always going to be a better shout unless you really want the iMac aesthetics.

The only other real viable option is the M5 Pro Mac mini. It's a chip with more CPU and GPU cores than the M6, and you can pay to go from a 15-CPU, 16-GPU core mix to an 18-CPU, 20-GPU version for just $200 more.
Its base configuration also starts with 24GB of memory and 512GB of storage. 2.5Gb Ethernet is now standard on the Mac mini, but 10Gb Ethernet is only $100 away.

For the rest of this budget range, the Mac mini M6 and M5 Pro are your only serious contenders. You'll generally fare better with the M6 and upgrades for general computing, versus the M5 Pro, which is the performance option here.
That is, until you need more than 32GB of memory, which the M6 Mac mini can go to. At $2,299, you've hit the maximum configuration of 32GB of memory and 2TB of storage for the M6 Mac mini.
For the same money, you can get the 15-core CPU M5 Pro chip, 48GB of memory, and 512GB of storage. It's the better bet, and still is at the top end of this range at $2,499.

At this point, you're going to be looking squarely at the M5 Pro Mac mini with the 18-core CPU upgrade, 512GB of storage, and 48GB of memory. For $100 more, you could keep the lower-tier chip and get 48GB of memory and 1TB of storage.
While the iMac range should not be a consideration, a serious contender becomes an option too.
$2,500 and beyond: M5 Pro Mac mini, Mac Studio
$2,499 is also the price for the lowest-priced Mac Studio. Equipped with the 18-core CPU and 32-core GPU M5 Max, it has 36GB of memory and 512GB of storage.
This is going to be the option to take if you need performance.

If you have another $300 to spend, making it $2,799, the next Mac Studio upgrade is storage to 1TB. The quoted $300 fee to upgrade to the 18-core CPU and 40-core GPU also means paying an extra $300 again for a memory upgrade, so it doesn't apply at this price point.
For the same money, you can get the upper-tier M5 Pro Mac mini with 48GB of memory and 1TB of storage. Or you can pay $100 more for the 64GB memory upgrade and 512GB storage instead.
The Mac Studio seems like the best option again.
Desktop Mac price ranges from $2,500 up, as of September 2026

At $3,099, you can get the M5 Max Mac Studio with the 40-core GPU option, as well as a 48GB memory upgrade and 512GB of storage. The $3,199 M5 Pro Mac mini can be configured with 64GB of memory instead, as well as more storage, but the far fewer GPU cores work against it here if performance is your thing.

The top configuration of the iMac exists here, with 2TB of storage, Nano-texture glass, the better chip, and 24GB of memory. A 32GB option is theoretically available at $3,299, but that is not currently sold by Apple.
The iMac exits the chat here, outclassed by all of the other options. That is, unless you desperately want an all-in-one Mac color-matched to a room.

We have also reached a point where the decisions become an awful lot easier to determine. Since the budget is so considerable, it becomes more about what you can do performance-wise, so chip performance and memory are priorities over storage.
Beyond this point, the M5 Pro Mac mini specs will lean towards using the best chip and the maximum 64GB of memory, with storage and the Ethernet upgrade being the only real upgrades.
Since you can still vary your chosen chip or memory on the M5 Max Mac Studio, that will be the best option to pick.
Mac Studio (2026)
The 2026 Mac Studio can be configured with an M5 Max or M5 Ultra chip, with a Neural Accelerator in each GPU core.
Buy at Adorama
Buy at B&H
Buy at Expercom

At $5,499, the Mac Studio with M5 Ultra becomes a possibility. The base configuration of a 30-core CPU and 64-core GPU is way more than what you can get from the M5 Pro Mac mini, by a considerable margin.

Storage at 1TB for the M5 Ultra is fine, but the base 96GB of memory is a big thing here. The M5 Pro Mac mini's nearest is all but the top spec at $4,799, with only the $2,000 jump from 4TB to 8TB left to go.
For the same $5,499, the M5 Max Mac Studio can be set to use the upper-tier chip that's still not Ultra good, but with 128GB of memory and 1TB of storage. The Ultra model is the best play again.

The Mac mini's last hurrah is at $6,799, with the upper-tier M5 Pro chip, 64GB of memory, and 8TB of storage. The M5 Max Mac Studio is still considerably better with its upper-tier chip, 128GB of memory, and 4TB of storage.

For the same price, the M5 Ultra Mac Studio's upper-tier 36-core CPU and 80-core GPU chip is the option to go for. Sure, it has 96GB of memory and 1TB of storage, but the sheer performance available to you is the draw here.

From here on up, the fight between the M5 Max and M5 Ultra versions of Mac Studio trades massive performance for storage capacity as the prices rise. A lot of that is storage on the M5 Max, which eventually hits its peak at $8,899.

That price level gets you to an M5 Max with an 18-core CPU, 40-core GPU, 128GB of memory, and 8TB of storage. You could instead get the M5 Ultra with the 36-core CPU, 80-core GPU, 96 GB of memory, 4TB of storage, and still save yourself $600.
Unless you really need that extra bit of memory, the M5 Ultra is still the better choice because of that performance.

From here on up, the M5 Ultra Mac Studio is the only choice, until it reaches its inevitable peak at $18,299. That insane price includes the upper-tier chip variant, as well as two key painful upgrades.
The first, and more necessary of the two, is the memory. Going from 96GB to 256GB is a scary $4,000 charge to your bank account.
The second is storage, as the upgrade cost from 8TB to 16GB alone is also $4,000.
Quite frankly, anyone buying for the performance of the M5 Ultra will see the memory upgrade as essential at this price level, but the storage isn't as necessary.
As discussed earlier, storage fees are something that can be mitigated by using external devices. When thousands of dollars are at stake, it's an option potential buyers will be keen to explore.

23b006e10aefe5daec40a03d.title: 苹果发了首款折叠屏iPhone Duo！却让人更怀念乔布斯了

units.text: 北京时间9月10日凌晨1点，苹果秋季产品发布会开始了。
苹果园区现场，灯光亮起，约翰·特努斯（John Ternus）站在舞台中央。他穿了件工装风格深色休闲夹克，不是乔布斯的黑高领，也不是库克的商务衬衫。一个做了二十多年硬件的工程师，延续了他一贯的工程师与务实风格，穿回了做硬件的衣服。
和现场观众不同，网上的观众看到了另一种开场。一段影片结尾，一辆汽车驶入了苹果公司，库克从黑暗中现身，他说“不，不，不是我”，然后引出特努斯出场。
特努斯没有沿用库克的“早上好”作为开场，首先感谢了团队，提了一嘴“制造世界上最好的产品”那个老使命。然后话锋一转，开始讲一个“智能个人中心”的概念。“世界上没有比iPhone更适合成为你智能个人中心的产品”，他用了大概七分钟，没讲任何参数，没展示任何硬件，只是重新定义iPhone在这个AI时代的位置。
整场发布会随一句“现在，它来了”开始。在随后的产品介绍环节，视频中的特努斯换了另一套衣服，深紫红色修身款的长袖圆领针织衫，下身穿着深色牛仔长裤。肢体语言比库克有弹性，身体微微前倾，像是在跟你面对面聊天。
发布会由他开场，随后各个业务的负责人轮番登场介绍不同的板块。这些负责人出现在不同的场景，有的通过动画demo展示，有的站在场景里介绍时身旁白色字母突出关键词，有的甚至直接在身边穿插了小剧场的表演。iPhone 18发布会，苹果到底有没有讲好AI故事？
苹果正在把“讲故事”的权力，交给业务各自的负责人。这样的转变不是个人审美问题。在这个舞台上，衣服扣子解到第几颗、PPT上放什么图，本质上都在悄悄告诉资本市场，苹果现在是一家什么样的公司，它正在面对什么样的时代。
然而，发布会开始后，苹果股价几乎在过山车，尤其是在宣布首款折叠屏手机 iPhone Duo的售价和销售日期后，苹果股价迎来当日低点，跌幅一度接近2%。但在发布会后不到一个小时又涨到当日最高价319.15美元，随后回落。收盘时，苹果股价为315.34美元，当日跌幅最终锁定在0.28%。
聚光灯下的帝国更迭：从黑毛衣到工装夹克
每一个关心科技的人，都没法拒绝苹果秋季发布会的开场。
乔布斯在台上的十三年，更像“布道”。那件三宅一生黑色高领毛衣、磨损的牛仔裤、新百伦运动鞋，是科技史上最反叛的一身行头。他喜欢把双手在胸前抱成个圈，像托着一个看不见的球。
他的PPT每页一件事。一张巨大的产品图，或者一个关键词，刺眼但简洁。对于产品介绍，他更像是在变魔术，突然间把电脑从牛皮纸袋里抽出来，告诉你世界要变了。
库克接棒之后，舞台上的疯劲退了，变成“开业绩会”。他一向不是那种靠穿搭吸引目光的人，深色牛仔裤、修身衬衫或者Polo衫，偶尔加个毛衣，毫无记忆点。他最爱做的动作是双手合十，语调温和、内敛。他很少亲自讲技术细节，更多是当主持，然后把时间分给各个业务副总裁。
只不过，库克时代，苹果的市值从3000多亿美元涨到4.6万亿美元。他从来没有在台上说过一句“改变了世界”，但他说的是“我们非常自豪”。
现在，特努斯是第三幕，“硬核匠人”登场。但所有人的目光并不在那件工装夹克上，都期待他能开启新的产品周期，优化组合抬升ASP。就在发布会前几周，苹果刚刚交出了季度营收创了历史新高的业绩报告，营收突破千亿美元，还有16%的增长，但股价却暴跌，财报发布后两天市值蒸发约4300亿美元。
一家公司业绩涨、股价崩，是因为市场从来不看过去，看的是未来。苹果给出的下一季度营收增速指引低于华尔街。供应链在恶化，内存价格暴涨，库克在告别电话会上把当前的内存市场形容为“百年一遇的洪水”。
这就是特努斯接手的局面。账面上一切完美，但市场已经提前在问，AI的故事在哪里？供应链的坑怎么填？你能拿出什么新东西？苹果目前的市盈率是36.25倍，标普500的平均水平连它的一半都不到。投资者愿意付这么贵的门票，并不是为了一台手机，而是期望特努斯能把苹果带到一个新维度。
用资本市场的话说，苹果现在是一个“将来时”的故事。发布会前，苹果已经开始下跌，“预期差”的戏码，已随着发布会同时开场。
截至北京时间9月10日6点，发布会结束后四个小时，苹果盘后交易微涨至317.06美元，涨幅为0.55%。
产品：硬核匠人的拆解现场
这场发布会，特努斯带着苹果的高管们花了一个多小时在台上拆产品。这是他的老本行，自2001年加入苹果后就先后负责过多款PC、iPad和AirPods产品的硬件工程。不过，与以往他负责讲解技术本身不同，这一次他更多的是承担串场的角色。
iPhone 18 Pro系列是第一个登场的。全系搭载A20 Pro芯片，采用台积电2nm制程工艺。副总裁Sribalan Santhanam在介绍时，展示了一张芯片剖面图，关键位置被重点标注了。苹果这次专门为端侧AI大模型重新设计了这块区域，目的就是让大模型在手机本地跑起来。
图片来源：发布会直播截图
A20 Pro的CPU比A19 Pro快了20%，GPU快了40%，算力翻倍。内存带宽多了50%。散热也跟着改了，采用了新的封装方式，均热板的表面积也提升了，并加入了新的材料。电池的续航时长也进一步增大。这些堆在一起，就是苹果为AI准备得最充分的新产品。
但对发布会后就想买到新品的消费者来说，价格上涨是一个坏消息。Pro起售价是9999元，Pro Max起售价为10999元人民币，起售价比上一代上涨了1000元。1TB和2TB存储版本价格上涨得更多，整体涨幅也比美元价格更高。
本场发布会的亮点是折叠屏手机，不过在其亮相前，苹果还发布了新款的智能手表和耳机。与手机不同，Apple Watch Series 12和Ultra 4的价格并没有变动，AirPods 5标准版甚至在增加了主动降噪功能后仍保持了原价，无线充电盒的版本甚至降价了。
折叠屏的出场相当隆重。视频中，特努斯站在剧场场景下，在一句经典的“One more thing”之后，一系列线稿演示的动画勾勒了折叠屏手机的设计。在介绍产品时，苹果两个高管同时出场，这是正常发布会仅有的一幕。
苹果并没有选择传闻中的Fold或者Ultra来命名折叠屏，最终被定为了iPhone Duo，当然这个名字也有KOL在社交媒体上爆料过。
起售价为15999元人民币，256GB起步，最高2TB。7.6英寸内屏，展开像一本小书；5.4英寸外屏，合上就是一部小手机，相当于iPhone 18 Pro 90%的屏幕显示面积。不过，价格并没有此前传言那么夸张，尺寸也要更小一些。
苹果两位核心高管，全球市场高级副总裁Greg “Joz” Joswia和软件工程高级副总裁Craig Federighi直到这一产品才出现参与讲解，他们展示了一系列产品特性和使用场景。
从演示来看，通过不同折叠方式，可以满足用户自拍需求，视频观看方式也随着屏幕变化，甚至你可以只把他当作一个简单的日历或者闹钟，这和国内厂商对折叠屏的演示有很大不同。
图片来源：发布会直播截图
IDC全球及中国副总裁王吉平告诉虎嗅，定价体现了苹果的策略，也就是用相对“温和”的起售价吸引眼球， 再通过高配版本拉升利润。
从具体价格来看，Duo的起售价高于小米“中折叠”的常规顶配版，同时最Duo顶配版低于华为新款“三折叠”的顶配。
王吉平表示，它既用起售价压制了小米的高配用户，又用顶配去抢华为次顶配的市场，在高价位区间的覆盖非常严密。不过，由于国行采用eSIM，这可能导致部分用户流向本土折叠屏。
此外，苹果也在这个产品做了一系列取舍。它又将触控ID引入了这个产品，无论开合都能便捷、安全和统一的方式进行身份验证。同时，苹果官宣支持Apple Pencil。在摄像头上，Duo只保留了两颗，使用了与18 Pro同款的4800万像素主摄和4800万像素超广角。
摄像头的妥协可能会让刚看完iPhone 18系列各种酷炫镜头拍摄样片的观众感到有些遗憾。不过，因双屏可折叠的设计，苹果称其解锁了其他iPhone无法实现的拍摄体验，比如自拍时可以在外屏预览拍摄效果，或者播放吸引被拍摄者注意的内容。
图片来源：发布会直播截图
相比18 Pro和Pro Max马上就可以预订不同，Duo要到10月16日才可以预订，并且要到10月23日才能发货，晚了一个多月，并且对Apple Pencil的支持也要更晚一些才可以。
然而，台下资本市场的反应，跟台上这种热乎劲儿完全是两码事。
逃不掉的“发布会魔咒”
特努斯在台上笑得温暖，那些手握资金的投资者，脑子里全是分时图的线条。
资本市场对特努斯的这场处女秀，再次上演了一场教科书级别的冷酷对峙。其实就在特努斯正式接过CEO权杖的当天，资本市场曾给过他一份短暂却豪华的“见面礼”。上任首日，苹果股价应声上涨近3%。
然而，随着发布会的尘埃落定，苹果股价再次陷入了经典的“发布会焦虑症”。收盘时，苹果股价最终以315.34美元收盘，微跌0.28%。
事实上，发布会开始前，就已经有券商开始评估新品的价值和风险，猜测股价的走势了。一位二级市场分析师给虎嗅了一份资料显示，从Pro价格的实际变化、折叠机的发售安排和量化表态，到特努斯演讲的叙事重心是什么，这些问题都在考察清单内。
“买入预期，卖出事实”，这个规律在苹果身上反复应验。只能说，这不是特努斯的问题，是这个公司的发布会已经变成了一种固定的市场行为模式。有分析师总结称，发布会前股价上涨，发布会后往往小幅“利好出尽”回调，30到60天内收复失地。
翻翻旧账就知道了。
2010年iPhone 4发布，那是乔布斯最后一次站在台上推出一款真正的“革命性”产品。视网膜屏幕、玻璃机身、陀螺仪，任何一个单项拿出来都能让同行失眠一整年。发布会结束后，紧接着“天线门”爆发了。用左手握手机，信号就会掉格，苹果却回应用户拿法不对。惹了众怒，股价跌了好几周。
2014年，库克掏出iPhone 6和初代Apple Watch。以长周期的视角来看，iPhone 6后来成了苹果历史上最赚钱的单品，在“超级换机潮”推动下，发布会后首个财务季度收获惊人的180亿美元净利润，Counterpoint数据显示，这一代产品全球累计销量达2.22亿台。这是因为大屏幕踩中了所有安卓用户换阵营的节点。
但那场发布会结束的当天晚上，资本市场只关注一件事，当听到备受期待的Apple Watch无法在圣诞黄金购物季上市、必须推迟到2015年初发货时，失望的避险资金在尾盘疯狂出逃，直接把股价砸到了三周新低。
现在回头看，那个失望只持续了一个季度，而且第二代出来五年后，苹果把整个瑞士钟表行业干翻了。然而交易大盘上的实时数字，从来不会替资本预支五年的耐心。
2017年iPhone X发布，开启全面屏时代，人脸识别替代了指纹，OLED屏幕第一次出现在iPhone上，苹果第一次把旗舰机做到接近1000美元。发布会还没结束，股价一度上涨将近3%，但尾盘阶段，有消息传出来Face ID的产能爬坡遇到困难，初期备货可能只有不到300万台。资本市场的反应快得吓人，从涨3%到跌1.5%，只用了不到半小时。
这些事说明一个道理，华尔街从来不为当下的精彩鼓掌，他们只为预期的差额买单。苹果的发布会之所以每次都变成“股价打折现场”，是因为它的预期管理能力太强了。强到发布会之前，所有人都已经把产品猜了个七七八八。等到真东西拿出来，没有任何“意外”，那“预期差”就是负的。
这次更甚，发布会前券商分析师、数码KOL这群人已经把要发布的内容猜得七七八八，甚至有深圳华强北供应链已经生产出相关配件。发布会盘前下跌，市场在用脚告诉大众，“我们准备好了，但我们要看看你拿出来的是不是跟传说的一样”。
发布会结束后发现，魔咒并没有解除。至于后续股价是否会回涨，仍有待观察特努斯是否能帮助苹果解决一系列困境。
灯光熄灭后的四道硬坎
发布会结束，灯光暗下来。特努斯走下舞台，回到后台。那个地方没有闪光灯，没有掌声，只有一堆等他作出决策的文件、一堆等他回复的邮件，以及四个绕不开的问题。
首当其冲的考验，是苹果必须补齐在生成式AI浪潮中的短板。受限于各地严苛的监管政策，苹果引以为傲的全新Siri和AI功能无法全球同步落地。
欧洲市场，苹果全新AI功能因为隐私法规没法同步上线。在中国市场情况更复杂，本土大模型已经跑得飞快，每个月都有新版本发布，苹果智能虽然已在网信办备案，但目前进展尚未有更新消息。
这些问题库克任内就在谈，但特努斯接手的时候，项目尚未落定。华尔街资深苹果分析师、深水资产管理公司分析师Gene Munster就曾在他的社交媒体上称，这两个市场（欧洲和中国）贡献了苹果近一半的营收，这意味着Siri AI营收的增长将呈错峰态势。
与此同时，苹果正遭遇着严重的供应链成本危机。全球内存芯片及核心零部件价格最近半年大幅度暴涨，这严重挤压了苹果的硬件利润空间。为了维持40%以上的毛利率，苹果不得不全面提高部分高配硬件的售价。
在全球宏观经济放缓的背景下，硬件涨价的直接后果，就是消费者换机周期的进一步拉长。特努斯如何在“保利润”和“冲销量”之间踩准平衡木，是摆在这位硬件工程师面前的第一道财务难题。
此外，库克留下了一个4.7万亿美元市值的庞然大物，但也留下了一个饱受诟病的“挤牙膏式创新”传统。分析师们都很清楚，渐进式的优秀已经不够了。特努斯需要证明自己不仅是一个合格的硬件总设计师，更是一个能引领下一次产业变革的掌舵人。他需要用真正的硬核技术，找回乔布斯时代那种让人惊叹的“技术惊喜感”。
图片来源：发布会直播截图
折叠屏就是那个试探。一位显示屏行业分析师告诉虎嗅，苹果等了八年才做，不只是为了等技术成熟，更是怕它吃掉iPad。
一块展开七八寸的屏，正好卡在手机和平板中间，定位上是天然的兄弟相争。苹果最后想通了一件事，高端市场已经被折叠屏拿下了一大块，如果苹果没有产品去卡住这个位置，中高端用户会慢慢转向华为和三星。折叠屏对苹果来说不是增量，是一场防御战。
更长远的隐忧则在于地缘政治与监管。库克时代最赚钱的服务业务正遭到全球反垄断监管的合围，随着老将的隐退，欧盟和美国法院正在强行介入，服务业务增速放缓让外界感到担忧。政治经验尚浅的特努斯，面对日益复杂的多边地缘博弈和关税壁垒，需要快速补课。
不过，库克已经在为这件事打补丁了。六个月前，苹果管理层组织架构变动，从Meta挖来的Jennifer Newstead已走马上任苹果总法律顾问，她有足够应对法律诉讼的经验，还擅长处理公司和国家层级冲突。
这四件事，每一件单独拎出来都够一个CEO忙活一整个任期，特努斯上任不到十天，四个全堆在他桌上。
发布会是他擅长的，首秀已经结束，利落的工装和温暖的微笑确实为他赢得了掌声。发布会之外的那些事，AI的追赶、成本的危机、创新的瓶颈、地缘的摩擦才是真正考验他的地方。
乔布斯用疯狂的个性把苹果拉了回来，库克用严谨的理性和数字为苹果修筑了坚固的护城河，而如今接棒的特努斯，必须在这些危机中，为苹果找到一条重塑未来的关键之路。
灯光暗示，他转身，往后台走。有人低下头看了一眼手机，屏幕留下跳动的股价。苹果的每一次交接，资本市场都只认一种语言，不是掌声，是股价。

5a9a5ac0a63128f0e1487331.discovery_title: iPhone Duo supports Apple Pencil with USB-C on both displays
5a9a5ac0a63128f0e1487331.raw_lead: Apple couldn't quite get Apple Pencil Pro to work with iPhone Duo, but Apple Pencil with USB-C pairs fine over a cable and brings its basic functions to iOS for the first time.
5a9a5ac0a63128f0e1487331.title: iPhone Duo supports Apple Pencil with USB-C on both displays

units.text: Apple couldn't quite get Apple Pencil Pro to work with iPhone Duo, but Apple Pencil with USB-C pairs fine over a cable and brings its basic functions to iOS for the first time.

A rumor in late August suggested Apple tried and failed to include support for Apple Pencil on its upcoming foldable. The issue was apparently with where the Apple Pencil would need to mount for charging interrupting the ease of opening and closing the device.

It would have been disappointing to get such a large display without Apple Pencil support, but Apple did find a way with iPhone Duo. The Apple Pencil with USB-C is compatible with iPhone Duo thanks to its ability to pair and charge over a cable.

Apple introduced the Apple Pencil with USB-C after announcing an iPad with a newly placed Center Stage selfie camera. The arrangement prevented the necessary magnets for the previous Apple Pencils from fitting, so Apple released a more universal stylus instead.

It lacks features like Double Tap and pressure sensitivity, though it does understand the device's tilt angle. Apple Pencil Pro introduced other features like Barrel Roll, but the USB-C model does support Apple Pencil hover on select iPad models.
It isn't specified if hover works on iPhone Duo.

Once the Apple Pencil with USB-C is paired with iPhone Duo, it should just work without any configuration. The battery can last 12 hours when used continuously, though battery life varies depending on use and standby times.

While it might be frustrating that there is nowhere to store the Apple Pencil when not in use, it can easily slip into a pocket. Also, expect third-party iPhone Duo case manufacturers to come up with clever case designs to store the Apple Pencil.
You can buy an Apple Pencil with USB-C today for $79 (discounted to $69 on Amazon). The iPhone Duo goes up for pre-order on October 16 starting at $1,999.

2257caf4b54964f7296ae615.discovery_title: Apple has altered course on using customer data to train its AI
2257caf4b54964f7296ae615.raw_lead: As it turns out, Apple realistically needs customer data to make Siri AI work well. So, starting with iOS 27, it is asking users to opt-in to training on your data.
2257caf4b54964f7296ae615.title: Apple has altered course on using customer data to train its AI

units.text: As it turns out, Apple realistically needs customer data to make Siri AI work well. So, starting with iOS 27, it is asking users to opt-in to training on your data.

A new section in the iOS 27 privacy policy shows that Apple has reversed its stance on using customers' data to train its AI models. Previously, the company assured customers that it had no need for customer data, and would figure out how to make Siri AI work well without it.

Apple maintains that it "takes steps to ensure that personal data is not stored or used by Apple." But as Heise points out, and Apple has said in the terms of service for a few years now, the audio material may be listened to by Apple employees after anonymization.
Currently, new feature is opt-in only. When iOS 27 rolls out on Monday, September 14, users will see a prompt that asks users to help improve the chatbot, with an agree or "not now" button.

It also admits that data collected may be reviewed by "review personnel." It is unclear if "review personnel" are Apple employees or a third-party company contracted to read conversation transcripts, as it has historically been.
The change is a big deal.
Apple has been trying to make Apple Intelligence less of the boogeyman that OpenAI's ChatGPT and Meta's MetaAI have become in the public eye.
Of course, Apple has been training its AI on user data for a while now. It just came up with a complex, yet controversial method to do so, dubbed Differential Privacy.

That method required Apple to provide artificial prompts it believes are popular and then look for pattern matches in user data analytics. Then, because of artificially injected noise and a threshold of needing hundreds of fragment matches, there wouldn't be any way to surface unique or individual-identifying prompts.
But when it comes to Siri AI queries, the company likely needs to actually hear how users are interfacing with the assistant. At least if it wants to remain competitive.

The timing is notable, as Apple's newest Apple Watch models are designed to continuously listen for conversations. Users can request a transcript of the previous 15 seconds at any time, with the audio purged after the transcript is generated.
Siri Recap can also provide users with summaries of conversations from throughout the day. Apple says the feature relies on Private Cloud Compute.
That raises questions about what data could eventually become eligible for Apple's AI training program. As of yet, Apple hasn't said Apple Watch conversation data will be included.
It was inevitable
Apple was always going to get to this point. It was never a matter of if, but rather a matter of when.

Apple has been behind in the artificial intelligence race for quite some time now. And to keep pace with the rest of its competitors, whether it's Meta or OpenAI or Anthropic, it needs to analyze what works and what doesn't work with Siri.
And, unfortunately, to do so, it's going to have to access data. If you allow it, your data, specifically.
Apple's betting that some users will opt in. However, with more and more people growing skeptical of AI, that may not be the safest bet.

I personally doubt that, at least in the medium-term, Apple will force every user to submit to The Data Harvest. I do suspect, though, that the company may force that option in the future if you wish to use Apple Intelligence.
The real question is whether or not Apple will allow Apple Intelligence to remain opt-in forever. And I grow increasingly concerned that, eventually, the company will stop giving users that choice.
Update September 14, 11:56 AM ET: Removed how to opt out, pending final iOS 27 release.

194f11ece70b91d6eeb18c44.discovery_title: SmartGym 8 brings natural-language workout creation, Siri AI integration - 9to5Mac
194f11ece70b91d6eeb18c44.raw_lead: SmartGym is out with a massive update today that introduces AI-powered workout creation, management, deeper Siri integration, and much more.
194f11ece70b91d6eeb18c44.title: SmartGym 8 brings natural-language workout creation, Siri AI integration - 9to5Mac

units.text: SmartGym is out with a massive update today that introduces AI-powered workout creation, management, deeper Siri integration, and several features that leverage the new possibilities of iOS 27, iPadOS, and watchOS 27. Here are the details.
I’ve written before about how much I like using SmartGym to track my exercise routine.

SmartGym is an Apple Design Award winner, and it doesn’t take long to see why. Developer Matt Abras is constantly changing, updating, and tweaking the app to make it easier and more streamlined to manage, track, and log gym sessions, improving on what has long been one of the most mature and useful gym-tracking apps on the App Store.
Today, SmartGym is getting one of its biggest updates ever. SmartGym 8 introduces SmartGym Intelligence, which is, in essence, the app’s own take on Private Cloud Compute.
SmartGym introduces its own Private Cloud Compute alternative
As Abras explains, SmartGym is currently not eligible to use Apple’s Private Cloud Compute through the new Foundation Models framework. So, he decided to build his own.

units.text: iPhone Duo Can Do Split View, But Not Like Your iPad
Apple's iPhone Duo is the first iPhone that can run two apps side by side, but anyone expecting the sort of freedom that Split View offers on iPad might want to temper their expectations.
Apple's iPhone Duo marketing materials talk up app pairs and side-by-side windows, but it doesn't mention anything about resizing them. There's a reason for that.

If you put two apps side by side on the iPhone Duo's 7.6-inch foldable display, you can't drag the divider between them to make one app take up more space than the other. It's a fixed 50/50 split, regardless.

That's likely to be a disappointment to anyone who's used Split View on the iPad. Indeed, iPad owners have been able to resize apps in Split View when in landscape mode ever since 2015 when iOS 9 introduced the feature.
So why does Apple not let you resize apps on the iPhone Duo? It's likely down to the device's display geometry.

Both the inner and outer displays share the same 1:1.4 aspect ratio, and each half of the inner display works out to roughly the same size and shape as the outer screen. So an even split gives each app a canvas it already has to support, with the divider sitting neatly on the fold. (The only exception to this, it seems, is when watching a TV show or movie above another app in portrait mode; based on Apple's promo videos, Apple TV content is shown in its proper aspect ratio and the lower app is allowed to rise above the fold.)

If you were able to drag the boundary around, not only would it create a bunch of in-between sizes that wouldn't fit neatly on the outer screen, it would also be a nightmare for developers to build support into their iPhone apps.

Despite the lack of resizing capability, the iPhone Duo's foldable screen still has a lot of benefits. It allows you to quickly swap between apps, open two windows of the same app, and have a conversation over Messages while looking at another app's content, in both landscape and portrait modes. You can also save pairs of apps to come back to later.
